rules.plain_words: SUPERSEDED by rules.verbatim for every item with fact_phrases (no free-form factual sentence at all). Any other word - a synonym of best / only ('alone', 'just', 'the one', 'the rest', 'other', 'exception', 'took gold', 'star'), an order or table word, a streak word ('kept', 'continued', 'extended', 'another', 'deepened'), an equality word ('same', 'matched', 'equaled'), an intensity verb ('surged', 'tanked', 'sold off', 'in the green', 'higher', 'lower'), a number word ('three'), a month ('in October'), 'every' / 'all' / 'each', an arrow / medal emoji, or > < = - makes the sentence need to be a claim phrase verbatim. Numbers and moves are tied to their subject: each number goes right after the company / sector it belongs to ('$MSFT −1.13%', never '$MSFT +2.03%' when +2.03% is $AAPL's), and rose / fell / up / down must match the move of every company / sector it is said of (never a move the item does not give, never negated, never with will / could / may).
rules.claims: superseded by claim_phrases (kept for the direction / date reading): comparatives and superlatives (led, biggest, largest, worst, best, most, least, only, first, top, #1, record, 'outperformed every other') only as the item's claims state them: name only that claim's companies / sectors in that sentence; each claim has a polarity (best = top gainer, worst = top loser, null = no side) and a rank (1 = its one subject is #1; group = its subjects are the top N in order) and a metric (usd_change, pct_change, market_cap, ...): say the side with the noun ('top loser', 'led the drop', 'biggest gainer'; 'top' / 'led' / '#1' alone or with an entity noun ('top sector', 'led its sector') read as best, whatever number stands beside them; with any other noun ('led the rout', 'top casualty') say best / worst instead), say the metric as the claim does (dollars vs percent vs market cap), the singular ('the biggest drop') only for the rank-1 subject, a list only from #1 in order, 'among the biggest' for other members, 'the two biggest' / 'one of the two biggest' only for the top 2; '#N by <metric>' only as the item's rank_by_usd / rank_by_cap / claims state it; 'of the 500' / 'overall' / 'of all' / 'on the day' only with a claim that has no within, 'of the 10' for the basket; a sector only as a sector claim (kind sector) says, a stock 'within' a sector only with that sector next to the word ('in Tech', 'Tech's', 'its sector'); a question is checked like a statement (only one about the reader, naming nothing, is exempt); 'did better than' / 'outperformed' / 'fell more than' compare percent unless dollars are named, and need a claim of that metric; rules.moves: each item's moves: numbers = the sign of every number it allows with one sign, subjects = the direction of every company / sector it describes; never put a gain word (rose, gained, up) beside a loss or a loss word beside a gain ('Energy fell 2.6%' when Energy rose)
